links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 10, Reading and Writing Files
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: filepaths, reading and writing text files, shelve and the quiz project.

links.title: pathlib — Object-oriented filesystem paths
links.why: Every Path attribute and method of the chapter and more: parts, glob patterns, mkdir, read_text and the 3.14 change to exists().

links.title: Built-in Functions (open)
links.why: The full account of open(): every mode, the encoding, errors and newline arguments and the file object types it returns.

links.title: io — Core tools for working with streams
links.why: Why the default encoding is the locale's, the advice to write encoding out and the opt-in EncodingWarning.

links.title: 7. Input and Output
links.why: The tutorial on reading and writing files: methods of file objects, with, and saving structured data with json.

links.title: os — Miscellaneous operating system interfaces
links.why: makedirs, chdir, getcwd and the fields of a stat result, including the change to st_ctime on Windows.

links.title: shelve — Python object persistence
links.why: How a shelf works, the writeback argument, the restrictions and the security warning about pickled values.

links.title: dbm — Interfaces to Unix “databases”
links.why: Which backend a new database uses and what files dbm.sqlite3 and dbm.dumb make.

links.title: json — JSON encoder and decoder
links.why: The format to use for plain data that other programs read, and how Python types map to JSON.

links.title: 8. Compound statements
links.why: The exact steps of the with statement, which guarantee that __exit__ is called.

links.title: PEP 686 – Make UTF-8 mode default
links.why: Why Python 3.15 makes UTF-8 the default encoding of open().

links.title: PEP 597 – Add optional EncodingWarning
links.why: The warning that finds every open() call that leaves the encoding out.

links.title: PEP 428 – The pathlib module – object-oriented filesystem paths
links.why: The design of pathlib: pure paths and concrete paths.

links.title: PEP 519 – Adding a file system path protocol
links.why: How path objects can be given to open() and to os functions that used to need strings.
